PC: Washes hands with soap and water or hand sanitizer
Positions patient appropriately Supine or lateral decubitus, head of bed elevated
Inspects abdominal wall Notes location of scars, cellulitis, and collateral veins
Percusses the abdomen Notes tympany vs dullness

Palpates the abdomen and selects site Palpates and notes lateral border of rectus and chooses site 2 fingerbreadths superior and 2 fingerbreadths medial to anterior iliac spine Unless contraindicated, chooses LLQ.
Confirms appropriateness of site using ultrasound Uses low frequency probe to confirm: Presence of ascites Lack of nearby bowel
Marks site with needle cap or sterile marker
Washes hands again with soap and water
Puts on cap and mask, and then sterile gloves Optional: Applies sterile or non-sterile gown
Cleans area with sterilizing solution (chlorhexidine/betadine) Must dispose of swab appropriately without contaminating sterile environment
Drapes the area
Sets up the kit (Yueh catheter) Appropriately draws lidocaine and ensures no air in syringe Attaches Yueh catheter or paracentesis needle to 35 CC syringe Has assistant confirm proper tubing set up
Uses lidocaine to anesthetize the skin (wheal) Uses smaller bore needle Constantly aspirates before injecting
Anesthetizes deeper If no peritoneal fluid obtained from initial anesthetic, switches to larger bore needle to anesthetize the peritoneum
Using the Yueh catheter/needle complex enters the skin while aspirating

Continues advancing the catheter/needle complex while aspirating until peritoneal fluid is aspirated Stops advancing the needle once peritoneal fluid is obtained Pulls off enough fluid for diagnostic studies
Advances the catheter over the needle until it is flush with the skin and withdraws the needle syringe unit
Maintains sterile technique Does not contaminate sterile field with unsterile equipment Keeps gloved hands sterile up until tubing is accessed
Connects the tubing to a 1 liter vacuum container or the vacuum apparatus connected to low wall suction
Withdraws catheter when drainage stops
Places dressing
Positions the patient with area up
Send fluid for diagnostic studies Always sends for cell count
SBP: Calls “time out” Confirms patient ID, procedure, and site by all members of team doing procedure and no allergy to local anesthetic
Cleans up Caps needles by sliding needle into cap on table using one hand, secures cap in place only once sure it is over the needle or Directly disposes of uncapped needles in sharps container
ICS: Obtains informed consent Appropriately names risks (ex: infection, bleeding, abdominal organ puncture, death) and benefits: (ex: diagnosis and/or therapeutic relief)
